review.reason: Read methods, simulations, and limitations. Teaches network effects while distinguishing projected savings from deployment evidence.

item.title: Spatially informed demand-side policies for green hydrogen diffusion in Europe
item.headline: Hydrogen support could go further when nearby users benefit too
item.authors: Christian Rumpelnik, Behnam Zakeri, and Kavita Surana
item.summary: Simulations suggest supporting well-connected hydrogen users could stretch subsidies further. The projections assume adoption resembles historical natural-gas power generation.

evidence.question: Can nearby users make hydrogen support more effective?
evidence.method: Historical adoption modelling, a network of 14,108 potential European users, and subsidy simulations through 2100.
evidence.limitations: An indirect cost measure and sector averages simplify real plants; savings are modelled.

explainer.finding: Adding a location-based criterion improved simulated auction cost-effectiveness by up to 15% through 2100.
explainer.method: Researchers compared subsidy allocation rules using adoption patterns estimated from gas plants.
explainer.meaning: Nearby factories could share infrastructure and expertise, helping additional users switch to hydrogen.
explainer.limits: Hydrogen may spread differently. Future costs and competing technologies remain uncertain; this does not demonstrate realized savings.
